pr.title: Sign off the release pull request's version bump in the Release workflow
pr.head: 9ee28134453fc0e8acfed8ec063d62e1358d9525

summary: Projector ships a release through its Release workflow. Someone starts the workflow by hand, its propose job raises the version in pyproject.toml and the two plugin manifests on a release/vX.Y.Z branch, and opens a pull request. Merging that pull request tags and publishes the release.

main has a ruleset that requires the projector/review commit status, which a clean Projector review posts on the head it reviewed. No review session picks up a pull request that the workflow's own token opened, so every release pull request waited for a review that never came.

This change has the propose job sign off its own commit. After the bump commit, it checks that the commit changes exactly the files in release.py's VERSION_FILES, and fails before the push when anything else changed. After the push, it posts a success projector/review status on that one commit. A later push to the release branch makes a new head with no status, which waits for a review like any other head.

The review found one problem: the guard checks only the release commit, not the commit the job started from. A run dispatched from a branch other than main carries that branch's commits into the release pull request, and the status signs them off as a version-only release.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Propose job: the Release workflow's job that runs on a manual dispatch and opens the release pull request.
  • projector/review: the commit status main's ruleset requires before a merge, normally posted by project review publish.
  • VERSION_FILES: the three files that carry Projector's version, listed in .github/scripts/release.py.

groups.title: The propose job signs off its version bump
groups.kicker: A guard on the release commit, then a success status on it
intro: The propose job gains statuses: write, the permission the commit statuses API needs. Its step now runs a guard between the commit and the force-push, and posts the status between the push and the pull request.

The guard lists the files the release commit changes, sorted, and compares them with the sorted VERSION_FILES that it imports from release.py. The status carries the description "Version-only release; needs no review" and links to the workflow run. The release pull request's body now says the workflow posted it.

files.note: The guard, the status post, and the permission for it.

checks.text: The review replayed the job's commit and guard in a clone of the head. A plain patch bump passes and lists the three version files, and a bump with README.md also changed exits 1 and names it.
The active Projector review ruleset requires the projector/review context from any source, with no bypass, so a status posted with the workflow's token satisfies it.

The guard compares HEAD^ with HEAD, and the job's if tests only the event, so a run dispatched from another branch, through Use workflow from or gh workflow run --ref, signs off every commit that branch has beyond main. In the review's replay, a branch with one extra commit passed the guard while the release branch also changed src/projector/__init__.py. Refusing any GITHUB_REF but refs/heads/main before the bump closes it.

files.note: The Release section now says the workflow posts the status and why a later push still needs a review.

checks.text: The fuller account of the Release workflow in docs/plugins.md, under "Release an update", explains the propose job's actions: write but does not yet mention the status or statuses: write. The review lists that as a suggestion.
